findings.problem: The app lesson a5-wrap step 'Adding up the cost' (js/content/algo/algo-p5-01.js line 354) says 'For 7 points and a hull of 5 that is 7+6+5+4+3 = 25 checks', and a bank question (js/bank/algo-71.js, a5-wrap) asks for the same total with answer 25. The real algorithm (the app's own 'Watch it run', and A5.WRAP) measures 6, 6, 5, 4, 3 candidates = 24, because round 1 does not test the start point against itself (the lesson's formula |S| - i + 1 counts h as a candidate). The video never shows a tally, but its fans do draw 6, 6, 5, 4, 3 rays, so anyone who counts them gets 24, not the lesson's 25.
findings.fix: Do not add a check tally to the video (or if one is added, say 24 and word it 'one sweep of the other points per corner'). Fix the lesson and bank at source: '6 + 6 + 5 + 4 + 3 = 24 checks' (or say 'about 25'), and change the bank question's answer/why to match. The video's A5.WRAP.checks already asserts 24.
findings.evidence: Re-ran the app's wrapRun logic in node (scratch app.js): candidates per round 6,6,5,4,3, total 24; common.js asserts WRAP.checks === 24. Stills s5@7.4 (6 rays from G), s5@8.6, s5@10.8, s5@12.2 show the shrinking fans.

findings.problem: Caption 2 'Every turn is a left turn.' (3.4-5.5) is only true for an ANTICLOCKWISE walk. Scene 5 then wraps the same hull CLOCKWISE (A G E D C), where every turn is a right turn, and the video never says so; the lesson (a5-or-2 predict, 5.1 step 'One-way turns') states 'always left or always right', and says gift wrapping keeps turning right. A first-time learner who has just been told 'hull = all left turns' can read gift wrapping's clockwise walk as contradicting it. The headline 'always turns the same way' is correct; the caption narrows it to left without the direction.
findings.fix: Caption: 'Walk anticlockwise: every turn is a left turn.' or the shorter 'Anticlockwise, every turn is left.'. In scene 5 add one short cue such as a 'clockwise' tag on the hull list or the caption 'Wrapping goes clockwise, so its turns are right turns.' Keep the 'all left turns' pill but label it 'anticlockwise: all left'.
findings.evidence: Still s4@5.2 (caption 'Every turn is a left turn.', 'all left turns' pill); s5@12.2 and s5@14.2 show the hull list A G E D C (clockwise order) with no direction word; A5.HULL_CW in common.js.

findings.problem: The key tag reads 'log n = 10' with no base. The lesson (5.6 'The tipping point') and bank use log2 (log2 1024 = 10). A learner who knows log as base 10 reads log 1,024 = 3.01, and the scan bar's 10,240 = 1,024 x 10 then does not check out.
findings.fix: Change the tag text to 'log₂ n = 10' (rendered a test in Nunito at 28 px: the subscript 2 glyph shows, small but legible) and the key 'scan: n log₂ n'; or write 'log n = 10 (base 2)'. Also use log₂ in the recap row 3 label if space allows ('cost n log n' is fine there).
findings.evidence: Still s8@4.8 / s8@11.4 show 'scan: n log n' and 'log n = 10'. Scratch test (stills/sub.png) with 'log₂ n = 10' renders cleanly. Lesson: algo-p5-x-02.js 'The tipping point' ('h ≈ log₂ n', 'log₂ n = 10').

findings.problem: The storyboard outline and lesson 5.6 make the TIPPING POINT the point of the lesson: wrapping wins while h < log2 n = 10, they tie at h = 10 (10,240 = 10,240), the scan wins above. The scene shows only the two extremes (h = 4 and h = 1,024), and the 'log n = 10' tag is orphaned: nothing on screen uses it to say where the crossover is. A learner is left with 'small hull: wrap, big hull: scan' but no idea how small (the recap also drops it).
findings.fix: After the ring verdict (about 10.7-11.6) add a short tag/caption 'wrap wins while h is below 10', or draw a small number line h = 4 ... 10 ... 1,024 with the tie marked at 10 (green left of it, red right). Reuse the existing 'log n = 10' tag as the bridge ('tie at h = log₂ n = 10').
findings.evidence: Outline in videos/_plan/algo-5.json ('wrapping wins while the hull is small (h below log2 n = 10)', 'they tie at h = 10'); A5.COST.tie = 10 is asserted but never drawn. Stills s8@4.8, s8@11.4: no mention of 10 as a threshold; captions at 5.1-6.6 'A small hull favours wrapping.' only.

findings.problem: Nothing in the video says WHERE n log n comes from. The storyboard outline says 'cost n log n, the sort dominates' and lesson 5.4 ('Where the time goes') explains: the sort costs n log n, the stack scan is one pass (each point pushed once, popped at most once, O(n)). In the video the scan appears only as a cost tag in scene 8 and in the recap, so 'scan: n log n' reads as a given and the viewer may think the stack pops are what cost n log n.
findings.fix: Scene 6: when the sorted row fills (about 6.0-7.0) add a purple tag 'sorting costs n log n'. Scene 7: final caption (13.3-14.9) 'The stack is the hull. One pass after the sort.' Scene 8 key: 'scan: sort + 1 pass' or 'scan: sort, n log n'.
findings.evidence: Captions in scenes 6 and 7 (stills s6@5.8, s7@14.5) contain no cost words; scene 8 key tags (s8@4.8) only say 'scan: n log n'. Outline text in algo-5.json; lesson algo-p5-02.js step 'Where the time goes'.

findings.problem: The claim 'the farthest pair is always two hull corners' is asserted but not shown. The scene drops the 11 pairs with an inside point FIRST (caption 'Drop pairs with an inside point.', 3.6-5.5) and only then highlights the longest of the 10 corner pairs (A-E). The viewer never sees that the longest of ALL 21 is also A-E (true: A-E 366.9, then A-D 270.7; the longest involving B or F is B-E 255.0), so the orange pair proves nothing and could look like a coincidence of the pairs that were kept. The lesson's reason (slide any point outwards and its distances only grow) is also absent.
findings.fix: Before the drop (about 3.0-3.5) pulse the longest of all 21 segments orange and tag it, then fade the inside-pair segments around it so it visibly survives; caption 'The longest pair is always between two corners, so inside points can go.' Optionally give the 11 dropped pairs a faint shorter look (A5.FAR.pairs[].len is available).
findings.evidence: Stills s9@2.0 (all grey), s9@4.4 (inside pairs fading, no highlighted pair), s9@7.0 (orange A-E only after the drop). Recomputed distances in node: AE 366.9, AD 270.7, BE 255.0; 11 non-corner pairs.

findings.problem: ALGO_RULES asks the title sub line to say what the algorithm CHANGED ('How Google ranks the web'). 'How to wrap a set of points' describes the mechanism, not the payoff; the lessons supply real payoffs (5.1: rangers estimating a habitat, a robot planning a safe path; 5.4: Bell Labs needing hulls of about 10,000 points in 1972; 5.8: farthest pair, clustering, separating classes, graphics) that never appear anywhere in the video.
findings.fix: Sub line such as 'How to draw the edge of any cloud of points' or 'The outline behind maps, robots and graphics'. If a payoff scene is wanted, scene 9's intro could name one lesson example (e.g. 'a ranger log of animal sightings').
findings.evidence: Still s1@2 (sub line 'How to wrap a set of points'); algo-5.json titleCard.sub; lesson algo-p5-x-01.js 'Why draw a boundary?' and algo-p5-02.js 'Why a second algorithm?'.

findings.problem: The outline's 'Not covered (lessons 5.5, 5.7 and the workshop)' list is incomplete. Also absent from the video: 5.1 step 1 (rangers/robot motivation), 5.2 steps 5-6 (y-down screens flip the sign; cross product = twice the signed area; inside test), 5.3 pseudocode (candidates = S minus H plus H[0]), 5.4 step 1 (Bell Labs, n^2 vs n log n for 10,000 points) and pseudocode, 5.6 interior elimination, 5.8 steps 2-4 (clustering, line separability, graphics/paths). None of these is a mistake, but the storyboard claims more coverage than delivered, and the y-up sign rule in scene 3 is never reconciled with the y-down screen the later scenes use ('left' means as seen on screen).
findings.fix: Update the outline's 'Not covered' list to match; optionally add a half-line in scene 3 ('y up, like a graph') so the sign rule is tied to the grid that is drawn.
findings.evidence: Compared lesson steps in js/content/algo/algo-p5-01.js, algo-p5-02.js, algo-p5-x-01.js, -x-02.js, -x-04.js with scene captions and the outline in algo-5.json.

findings.problem: Rounds 2-5 show a fan of dashed rays and an orange winner but no criterion: the caption 'Smallest angle wins' belongs to round 1 only and the later angles (180-360 degrees, measured from the previous corner) are deliberately hidden. So the winners E, D, C, A are true (re-run in node) but unverifiable by eye, and 'Repeat from each new point.' does not say what is repeated.
findings.fix: Caption 4: 'Same test from each corner: the smallest swing wins.' Optionally re-run the purple sweeping line (no numbers) in round 2 so the winner is the first ray touched, as in round 1.
findings.evidence: Stills s5@7.4, s5@8.6, s5@10.8 (fans with no angles); app wrapRun re-run: G->E A360 B347 C329 D286 E250 F306, E->D, D->C, C->A.

findings.problem: The reference point 'r' is just a purple dot labelled 'r' (1.9-6.0). The lesson stresses that r is MADE UP and not in the data (its own quick check asks why). With the video stating '7 points' in scene 9, 'r' can read as an eighth point.
findings.fix: Label it 'r (made up)' or add to caption 1: 'A made-up point r gives the angle a start.'
findings.evidence: Stills s5@3.7, s5@4.2 show the r disc above A with no explanation; lesson algo-p5-01.js 'Start somewhere guaranteed'.

findings.problem: The 'sweeps' counter counts COMPLETED sweeps: it reads 0 during the whole round 1 sweep (3.0-6.2), and 2 while the third sweep ('from E') is in progress at s5@8.6. The word sweeps next to 'from E' invites reading it as the current sweep number.
findings.fix: Either count the sweep when it starts (1 at 3.0, 2 at 6.6, ...) or relabel 'corners found'.
findings.evidence: Stills s5@4.2 (sweeps 0 with the finished 43 degree sweep), s5@8.6 (sweeps 2, from E).

findings.problem: The turn-log arrow for a corner draws on when the walker ARRIVES at that corner (arrive(i)), before it has turned; a turn at C needs the next edge C->D. Arrow 'A' (the closing turn G-A-C) is drawn when the walker reaches A, before it has gone on to C.
findings.fix: Delay each log arrow by about 0.25 s so it appears as the walker leaves the corner (arrive(i) + 0.25).
findings.evidence: Still s4@3.0: walker between D and E, arrow D still drawing; scene-04-dent.js lines with L5.drawOn(g, ramp(t, arrive(i), arrive(i) + 0.4)).

findings.problem: Caption 1 'Push the first two points.' is ambiguous: the first two points of the sorted row are D and E, but the scene (correctly, as in the app and lesson 5.4) pushes the LOWEST point C and the first sorted point D. Caption 2 'Left keeps the point' does not say which point (the middle one, t); the lesson's rule is 'right turn OR straight pops', but straight is intentionally not covered.
findings.fix: Caption 1: 'Start the stack with C and D.' Caption 2: 'Left turn: keep the middle point.'
findings.evidence: Still s7@1.5 (stack C, D; sorted row starts D E F ...); lesson algo-p5-02.js 'The stack pops dents'.

findings.problem: Three small accuracy points: (1) the dot clouds have 60 and 48 dots but are tagged n = 1,024 points and h = 1,024 corners (only the tags carry the numbers; never said that the pictures are samples). (2) The wrap bar counts up while growing, so a frame shows a non-result such as 1,037,069 (s8@9.0) before settling on 1,048,576. (3) The tags and captions state exact 4,096 and 10,240 'steps'; the lesson words them 'about n x h' and 'about n log n'.
findings.fix: Add a small 'picture of the shape' note or say 'every dot a point' only for the legend; hold the count-up so the bar number is shown only once it has settled (or use the final value from the start); use 'about' / '~' in the first caption ('Wrapping: about 4,096 steps').
findings.evidence: Stills s8@9.0 (1,037,069 on a grey bar), s8@10.6 (48-dot ring, 'h = 1,024 corners'), s8@4.8 (60-dot blob, 'n = 1,024 points').

findings.problem: Headline 'The cost depends on the size of the hull' is true of wrapping only; the scan's cost does not depend on the hull at all (that is the point of the scene). It can be read as 'both costs depend on the hull'.
findings.fix: Headline: 'Wrap or scan? It depends on the hull' or 'Which is cheaper depends on the hull'.
findings.evidence: Scene title in scene-08-cost.js; stills s8@4.8 and s8@10.6 show the scan bar unchanged at 10,240.

findings.problem: The convex test only ever succeeds: A-D, G-D and B-F all stay inside, and 'convex?' flips to 'convex' by construction (the shape is the hull). The lesson's contrast (an L-shaped set where the segment leaves the shape) is missing, so a first-time learner never sees what would make a shape NOT convex.
findings.fix: Optional: before the three green segments, flash a small dented shape with one red segment that leaves it, or add a red 'not convex' counter-example to the left of the band for a second.
findings.evidence: Still s2@10.4 (blue B-F segment growing, two green ticks) and s2@11.9; lesson algo-p5-x-01.js 'Convex: the segment test' (convex and not convex frames).
